summary: لغو (laghw) refers to speech or actions that are vain, idle, or of no real account. It signifies something unprofitable or useless, often without serious intent.
lane: لَغْوٌ ذ , applied to speech, &c., Nought; of no account; (M, K;) unprofitable. (M.) -b2- اليَمِينُ اللَّغْوُ : see KT, voce يَمِينٌ .

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: لَاغَاهُ He jested, or joked, with him; inf. n. مُلَاغَاةٌ . (A, TA.) You say, لَاغَاهُ فِى البَيْعِ . (A, TA, art. كيس .)
لَغْوٌ , applied to speech, &c., Nought; of no account; (M, K;) unprofitable. (M.) اليَمِينُ اللَّغْوُ : see KT, voce يَمِينٌ .

headwords.gloss: The genuine language; the classical language
headwords.def: اللُّغَةُ The genuine language of the Arabs; which is the classical language.

headwords.gloss: Of; relating to, the genuine language; A genuine lexicological meaning
headwords.def: لُغَوِىٌّ Of, or relating to, the genuine language of the Arabs. مَعْنًى لُغَوِىٌّ A genuine lexicological meaning.
لُغَيَّةٌ A word of weak authority. (TA, voce جِرَاب , et passim.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
